newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ZLOTY STRONGER VS BASKET, T/N BIDS JUST UP.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ZLOTY STRONGER VS BASKET, T/N BIDS JUST UP.

text.p: The Polish zloty firmed against the basket of currencies despite a dollar jump against the mark, likely underpinned by foreign buying of Polish longer- term paper, dealers said.
Some said the purchases may have been sparked by weakening expectations of a possible official interest rise as foreigners try to buy at top rates on the secondary market.
"Foreign interest in Polish treasuries may have risen after the deputy central banker said there were no clear signals as yet for or against a rate rise," said a dealer at a major Polish bank.

The zloty closed at 3.24/3.20 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Friday's 3.12/3.10 percent. It closed at 2.9040/50 to the dollar, down from 2.8955/60 on Friday and at 1.8287/94 to the mark, up from 1.8356/62.
Dealers estimated foreign investment at Monday's one- billion zloty primary T-bill tender as small, but said they bought some 75-100 million zlotys of Polish T-bonds last week.
"Foreign investors bought an estimated 75 to 100 million zlotys of two-year and five-year fixed bonds in secondary trade over last week," a dealer at a foreign bank in Warsaw said.
Two-year bonds were at 20.60-40 percent on the secondary market on Monday and five-year paper was around 19.70 percent.
Overnight deposit rates closed at 21.50/21.70 percent down 0.10 point from opening and tomorrow/next were at 21.65/21.80 percent, just up at bid from 21.55/21.80 percent.
Minimum prices of all T-bills fell at today's primary auction on total demand of 549 million zlotys against a one billion zloty offer. The treasury sold bills worth 386 million.
